messages:
maria_g: :rotating_light: Seeing a P99 inference latency spike in eastus2 starting ~23:08 UTC. Graphs show sudden tail latency and packet retransmits from several GPU hosts. Suspect a host-level QoS change (tc) landed earlier today. Link: https://graph.redwood/internal/infer/p99?range=1h

dmitri: which hosts / which qdisc? can you paste the tc output from one of the affected nodes?

maria_g: grabbed one host (gpu-node-12). output below. this host handles small synchronous connections for our realtime model.

```
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 8001: limit 1000p flow_limit 1024 quantum 1514 target 5.0ms interval 100.0ms
 Sent 12345678 bytes 12345 pkts (dropped 348, overlimits 92 requeues 5)
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
qdisc tbf 1: root refcnt 2 rate 1gbit burst 512b latency 50.0ms
 Sent 98765432 bytes 98765 pkts (dropped 1245, overlimits 124)
```

maria_g: note the tbf burst is 512b on this host; that seems extremely small for many small flows and causes taildrop under bursty RPC patterns.

ajay: that 512b burst looks like the config from the new qos-daemon rollout (ansible role qos/2026-03-17). I flagged the template as conservative for bandwidth, but burst should've been 128kb in staging. wonder why prod got 512b.

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-17T20:10Z applied to env=prod-eastus2 by pipeline qos-rollout v1.3.2 (ansible playbook: roles/qos/tasks/main.yml).

oncall: maria, can you confirm whether RDMA (ib0) flows are affected or only eth0? we use SR-IOV on eth0 but some hosts also carry ib traffic for model shards.

maria_g: checked ib0 on same host — no qdisc applied there, RDMA counters look normal. drops are on eth0 and align with TCP retransmits in agent logs. inference SLOs degraded for sync clients.

leah: reproducing quickly on a canary host: when burst=512b I see sub-ms RPCs become 5-50ms and p99 jumps. increasing burst to 64kb improves tail significantly.

ajay: opened PR to fix ansible template to default burst=64kb and to gate rollout with a per-host flow-profile check: https://git.redwood/qos/PR-457. but we should rollback the prod change first.

oncall: agreed. @leah can you push a rollback for qos-daemon v1.3.1 to eastus2? escalate if any host doesn't converge.

leah: rolling back now to v1.3.1 on prod-eastus2 (starting with the 12 affected hosts). running: `ansible-playbook rollback-qos.yml -l prod-eastus2 -e qos_version=1.3.1`

infra-bot: rollback job started 1955004400: rolling back qos-daemon to v1.3.1 on 12 hosts.

maria_g: after rollback on gpu-node-12, quick metrics: p99 for that host back to baseline in ~20s. no more taildrops in tc counters.

leah: confirmed across the batch: drops down, retransmits normalized, global p99 for the service dropped from 320ms -> 18ms within 60s of rollback.

ajay: root cause: ansible templating bug — unit suffix parsed wrong, resulting in burst set to 512 (bytes) instead of 64k (kB). adding unit tests + CI lint to prevent & adding a staged canary of 2 hosts before fleet rollouts. PR updated.

dmitri: can we add a monitoring alert for sudden change in qdisc drop count or an automated preflight that compares planned qdisc params to expected profile? we should fail upgrade if burst < flow_profile_min.

maria_g: +1. also adding a synthetic small-RPC probe to the inference health checks so we detect tail latency from host-level QoS quickly.

oncall: good runbook updates: 1) how to verify tc outputs, 2) rollback command, 3) verify metrics after rollback. i'll file the postmortem and link to PR + graphs. tagging SLO owners. :white_check_mark:

leah: anything else we should do short term? we should scan other regions for same bad template substitution.

ajay: starting a sweep over prod fleets to look for burst < 8kb and flag. kicking off ansible --check first.

maria_g: thanks team — SLOs recovered. postmortem + remediation steps incoming in #postmortems.
